core.title: A Multi-Source Urban Water Quality Dataset for Seasonal Analysis
core.description: This data paper describes the construction, quality control, and reuse scenarios of a multi-source urban water quality dataset collected from 18 monitoring sites.
funders: National Natural Science Foundation of China, NSFC-2024-1007

data_paper_content_information.Title: A Multi-Source Urban Water Quality Dataset for Seasonal Analysis
data_paper_content_information.Abstract: The paper introduces monthly water-quality observations collected between March 2022 and February 2024 from upstream, midstream, and downstream monitoring sites. It documents sampling procedures, calibration logs, sensor metadata, and data-quality rules.

Dataset Basic Information.Title: Urban Water Quality Monitoring Dataset 2022-2024
Dataset Basic Information.Abstract: A dataset containing pH, dissolved oxygen, conductivity, turbidity, nitrate, phosphate, ammonia nitrogen, and temperature measurements for 18 monitoring sites.

Scope.Spatial Range: 18 monitoring sites across upstream, midstream, and downstream urban river segments

Dataset Basic Information.File Content: CSV measurement tables, XLSX sampling schedule, JSON sensor metadata, TXT calibration logs, README, and variable dictionary.

Dataset Authors.Contribution: Field sampling, instrument calibration, data curation, and dataset documentation.
Dataset Authors.Biography: The dataset authors specialize in environmental monitoring, urban hydrology, and reusable scientific data publishing.

data_paper_content_information.Introduction: Urban river systems show strong seasonal and spatial variation. The paper explains why a harmonized open dataset is useful for reproducibility studies and baseline model training.
data_paper_content_information.Data Collection and Processing Methods: Samples were collected monthly. Measurements were calibrated with standard buffer solutions and processed through unit normalization, timestamp alignment, duplicate removal, and automated range checks.
data_paper_content_information.Data Sample Description: Each record includes site identifier, sample time, river segment, coordinates, meteorological context, measured variables, instrument identifier, and quality-control flag.
data_paper_content_information.Data Quality Control and Evaluation: Quality control followed a two-stage process with manual review and automated outlier detection. Suspicious readings were retained with flags rather than silently removed.
data_paper_content_information.Data Use Methods and Recommendations: Users should filter by quality-control flags for trend analysis and cite both the article and the dataset. Missing values are marked as NA.
References: APHA. Standard Methods for the Examination of Water and Wastewater.
Wang et al. Urban river water-quality monitoring with sensor networks.
data_paper_content_information.Acknowledgements: The authors thank field technicians and local environmental agencies for site access and instrument maintenance.

Data Paper Authors.Contribution: Paper writing, data validation, statistical analysis, and repository preparation.
Data Paper Authors.Biography: The authors work on open environmental data, water-quality analytics, and urban sensing infrastructure.

data_paper_service_information.Data Paper Citation: Li M.; Chen Y.; Wang T.; Zhang E. A Multi-Source Urban Water Quality Dataset for Seasonal Analysis. Journal of Environmental Data Science, 2026.
